shared:
The Wulfen is a Clan Wolf light OmniMech designed in 3137 at the W-7 Facilities on Tamar as the Clan prepared to abandon its original Occupation Zone. Intended as a signature platform for ristar MechWarriors fighting Trials over contested resources and territory, the thirty-ton design fills the role of an exceptionally fast stealth combatant capable of dictating the terms of any engagement. The Wulfen leverages a blend of advanced Clan and Inner Sphere technologies, an unusual combination that reflects Clan Wolf's pragmatic approach to military procurement during a period of rapid territorial upheaval.

Despite early controversy within the warrior caste over its mixed-technology construction, the Wulfen quickly proved itself in combat and earned a reputation as a premier light OmniMech reserved for the Clan's most promising warriors.

The Wulfen's defining characteristic is its combination of extraordinary speed and battlefield invisibility. A Model 39b 300-rated extra-extralight engine propels the thirty-ton chassis to speeds exceeding 160 kilometers per hour, while six and a half tons of Imstar V-Stealth armor and an integrated ECM suite allow it to dictate engagements on its own terms. The use of mixed Clan and Inner Sphere technology (including an Inner Sphere XL gyro and Process 12 endo steel internals) frees ten tons of pod space for mission-specific loadouts, a generous allocation for a light design.

The Prime configuration pairs an Ultra Autocannon/2 with an ATM-3 system, providing flexible engagement options across multiple range brackets. Both weapons carry CASE II-protected ammunition, and a half-ton cargo pod offers modest logistical utility. Standard configurations emphasize the Wulfen's strengths as a long-range harasser and reconnaissance platform, though close-in variants mounting heavy lasers demonstrate the chassis's adaptability.

The Wulfen's principal vulnerability lies in its reliance on the extra-extralight engine, which makes the design exceptionally fragile if stealth protection is compromised. A single critical hit to either side torso can destroy the engine, making the Wulfen's survival dependent on maintaining its electronic and physical concealment.

The Wulfen's introduction was marked by controversy within Clan Wolf's warrior caste. Star Colonel Josiah Ward publicly denounced the design as tainted by Spheroid dishonor shortly after the first prototypes emerged from the W-7 Facilities, a statement widely interpreted as a political attack on Khan Seth Ward. SaKhan Garner Kerensky answered the challenge by forcing Ward to a Trial of Grievance, personally piloting a Wulfen prototype against Ward's Loki on the trial grounds outside Krefeld. Despite expectations that Ward's superior firepower would prevail, Kerensky used the Wulfen's mobility to control range and systematically dismantled the heavier 'Mech with precise long-range fire. The configuration Kerensky employed became the basis of the B configuration, and open complaints about the unit ceased.

Muted acceptance became admiration as the prototype Wulfen proved itself in combat during the Wolf Empire's invasions of the Republic of the Sphere, Free Worlds League, and Lyran Commonwealth. The few prototypes available when Clan Wolf uprooted itself demonstrated devastating effectiveness against the Silver Hawk Irregulars across half a dozen worlds during the invasion of the Marik-Stewart Commonwealth. The design further distinguished itself by outflanking the First Covenant Guards on New Olympia, an engagement that contributed to the death of former Paladin Thaddeus Marik.

Success in the field bred demand that far outstripped supply, prompting Clan Wolf to invest heavily in expanding production capacity and taking considerable measures to prevent Wulfens from being claimed as salvage or isorla. By the time the Wolves turned on their erstwhile Lyran allies, the Wulfen had cemented its status as the symbol of the ristar within the Wolf Empire's touman, reserved for frontline Galaxies and the Clan's most promising warriors.

text.overview: The Wolverine traces its origins to the earliest days of BattleMech development, when Norse BattleMech Works of Marduk designed the prototype WVR-1R in 2471 for the Armed Forces of the Federated Suns. Intended as a versatile front-line combatant emphasizing maneuverability and balanced firepower, the Wolverine filled a crucial role as a heavy scout and cavalry 'Mech capable of operating independently or as part of larger formations. When Kallon Industries acquired production rights and introduced the definitive WVR-6R in 2575, the design became one of the most widely produced medium BattleMechs in the Inner Sphere. Manufactured on multiple worlds by firms including Kallon Industries, Victory Industries, and Free Worlds Defense Industries, the Wolverine has served in every major conflict from the Age of War through the ilClan era. Its enduring success stems from a design philosophy that prioritizes versatility over specialization, making it equally effective as a scout, skirmisher, and striker.
text.capabilities:
The Wolverine's effectiveness stems from its well-balanced combination of firepower, mobility, and protection. The definitive WVR-6R mounts an Imperator-A autocannon/5 as its primary weapon, providing consistent medium-range fire support, complemented by a Holly short-range missile six-pack for close-quarters engagements and a single Magna Mk II medium laser in the head for additional punch. This weapons mix gives the Wolverine reliable engagement options across multiple ranges without generating excessive heat, a critical advantage during sustained operations.

Jump jets manufactured by Northrup provide a 120-meter jump capability, granting tactical mobility that allows the Wolverine to navigate difficult terrain and leverage advantageous firing positions. The chassis carries nine and a half tons of Maximillian 60 armor, providing excellent protection for its weight class and allowing the Wolverine to absorb punishment that would cripple lighter scouts. While the design's 86.4 kilometer-per-hour ground speed has occasionally been criticized as somewhat lacking for a dedicated reconnaissance platform, it remains adequate for the combined-arms skirmisher role in which the Wolverine excels.

The integrated Garret T11-b communication system and Sync Tracker targeting-tracking system give the Wolverine above-average command and control capabilities, making it a natural choice for lance and company command 'Mechs. This combination of respectable firepower, solid protection, and strong electronics has made the Wolverine particularly favored by Houses Davion, Kurita, and Marik, each of whom has developed specialized variants tailored to their tactical doctrines.
text.deployment: Developed independently by Taurus Territorial Industries, this Periphery variant represents the Taurian Concordat's adaptation of older Wolverine models for local requirements rather than a direct derivative of the mainline Federated Suns production. The most significant modification splits the standard SRM-6 launcher into three smaller launchers, distributing the missile capability across the chassis for improved tactical flexibility. The Taurian engineers also redistributed the armor scheme, reinforcing the center torso and legs at the expense of other locations to improve survivability in the close-range engagements typical of Periphery warfare. This independent development path reflects the Concordat's long tradition of modifying existing designs to suit their defensive doctrine rather than developing entirely new platforms.
text.battleHistory:
The Wolverine's story begins in the tumult of the Age of War, when the Federated Suns sought a new front-line BattleMech to bolster its border defenses. Norse BattleMech Works won the Capellan March contract, delivering the first four WVR-1R prototypes to Prince Varnay in 2471 and earning the design the informal nickname "Varnay-1R" among early pilots. The initial Wolverine emphasized rugged construction and close-combat capability, with engineers choosing heavy armor plating over more exotic weapons systems after initial experiments with particle projection cannons proved problematic due to overheating and electromagnetic interference with onboard systems.

The design underwent steady refinement over the following century. The WVR-3R appeared in 2490, incorporating incremental improvements, but it was not until Kallon Industries purchased production rights and introduced the WVR-6R in 2575 that the Wolverine reached its definitive form. The WVR-6R became a staple of the Star League Defense Force, with Kallon's factories on Nanking and Thermopolis producing thousands of units alongside facilities operated by Free Worlds Defense Industries on Gibson and Victory Industries on Marduk. Ironically, the Wolverine's proven design would serve as the template for Hegemony engineers' later upgrades to the competing Griffin and Shadow Hawk chassis, cementing its influence across the iconic fifty-five-ton medium 'Mech trio.

During the Succession Wars, the Wolverine became particularly associated with the Free Worlds League Military, which fielded the largest concentration of the design. The Fourth Succession War dramatically reshuffled production, as the Capellan Confederation lost control of the Nanking facility to the Federated Commonwealth while the Draconis Combine captured Victory Industries' Marduk plant. These shifts drove the development of faction-specific variants as each Great House sought to tailor the Wolverine to their own strategic needs, with House Kurita, House Davion, and House Marik all producing distinctive modifications reflecting their particular combat philosophies.

The Clan Invasion and subsequent technological renaissance sparked a new wave of Wolverine development. Multiple manufacturers introduced upgraded variants incorporating recovered Star League technology and newly developed weapons systems. The WVR-7K proved spectacularly successful in Kuritan service, inspiring Victory Industries' Project Phoenix modernization program, while the Davion WVR-7D took a more haphazard approach to upgrades before being refined through the same initiative. The Jihad era saw both Word of Blake-influenced designs and resistance variants enter service, with the WVR-9M especially emerging as a field modification used by Duchess Alys Rousset-Marik's freedom fighters before Kallon Industries adopted it for formal production at Thermopolis.

The post-Jihad period brought significant changes to Wolverine manufacturing. Luthien Armor Works secured licensing rights that shifted substantial production toward the Draconis Combine, while Kallon Industries' Nanking facility was rebuilt under Republic of the Sphere auspices. The ilClan era produced perhaps the most dramatic development in the Wolverine's long history when Clan Wolf seized the Thermopolis facility and converted its production lines to manufacture the Conjurer, the Clan design originally built from the Wolverine chassis. Despite this loss, manufacturers across the Inner Sphere continue to produce the Wolverine in significant numbers, ensuring the venerable design remains a fixture of medium 'Mech lances from the Periphery to Terra itself.

text.overview:
The Wraith was introduced in 3055 by Curtiss Militech, a little-known military technologies division of Curtiss Hydroponics, a Free Worlds League water purification company. Seeking to diversify into more profitable markets, Curtiss formed the division to leverage recovered technology and produce state-of-the-art military hardware. The resulting TR1 Wraith defied skeptics who dismissed it as little more than a walking water cooler. Built around one of the largest extralight engines ever fitted to a medium chassis, the fifty-five-ton Wraith prioritized speed and agility above all else, filling the role of a fast raider and scout hunter.

Its pulse laser armament complemented its jump-heavy combat doctrine, and the design proved surprisingly resilient for its weight class. Following the destruction of the Curtiss Militech factory on Paradise during the Jihad, the Wraith's production rights were acquired by Hellespont Industries on Sian, ensuring the design's continued service within the Capellan Confederation.
text.capabilities:
Speed and maneuverability are the keystones of the Wraith's design. Weapons and armor came secondary to cramming the massive LTV 385 XL engine into a medium chassis, granting the 'Mech a top speed approaching 119 kilometers per hour. Seven CurtissJet jump jets provide an impressive 210-meter jump capability, allowing the Wraith to outmaneuver most BattleMechs in existence and traverse difficult terrain with ease.

The Wraith's armament centers on Tronel pulse lasers, a deliberate choice that compensates for the accuracy penalties inherent in its jump-intensive combat style. A Tronel XIII large pulse laser serves as the primary weapon, backed by a pair of Tronel XII medium pulse lasers for close engagements. This all-energy loadout eliminates ammunition dependence, a significant logistical advantage for a design intended to operate independently on extended raids.

The 'Mech carries over eight tons of Kallon FWL Special ferro-fibrous armor, respectable protection for a medium design, though the cramped internal layout resulting from the oversized engine and endo steel structure makes battlefield repairs notoriously difficult. Curtiss addressed early maintenance concerns by providing a liberal warranty and producing replacement parts alongside each unit, though this did little to endear the design to field technicians.
text.deployment: Debuting in the Tennessee Valley arena in 3141, this custom variant was developed by Team New World on Solaris VII. Clan ferro-lamellor armor provides exceptional resistance to nearly all forms of damage, while a Clan-specification XL engine improves durability over the original powerplant. MASC enables even greater bursts of speed, and four Clan extended-range medium lasers replace the entire original weapons suite, delivering more firepower at greater range. A hatchet adds a melee dimension suited to arena combat, quickly earning the nickname of a tomahawk among the stable's fanbase.
text.battleHistory:
Curtiss Hydroponics had been a household name in the Free Worlds League for generations, manufacturing water purification systems that served communities across the nation. By the mid-3050s, however, spiraling costs and declining profits left the company searching for new revenue streams. The formation of Curtiss Militech, a military technologies division devoted to producing state-of-the-art BattleMech hardware using recovered technology, was met with open skepticism from the defense industry. Analysts who had scoffed at the idea of a water purification company entering the military market were forced to reconsider when the TR1 Wraith debuted in 3055, a design far removed from the "water cooler on legs" many had predicted.

The Wraith found an immediate audience among independent MechWarriors and mercenary commands who valued its exceptional speed and ammunition-independent weapons loadout. Early operational experience revealed that the design was more difficult to employ effectively than its raw specifications suggested. Commanders frequently compared the Wraith to the Charger, noting that while both designs possessed impressive speed and durability for their weight class, the Wraith's short-ranged pulse lasers left it ill-suited to line combat or traditional scouting roles. It lacked the reach to engage lighter scout hunters at range, yet carried too little firepower to serve as a frontline combatant.

Over time, tactical doctrine evolved to match the Wraith's unique capabilities. Commanders began assigning the design to skirmisher and fast raider roles, where its speed allowed it to strike and withdraw before heavier opponents could respond. Free Worlds League units along the Marik-Steiner border struggled to find a niche for the design, but Curtiss found greater success selling on the general market. The Capellan Confederation, Draconis Combine, and Word of Blake all purchased the Wraith, as did numerous mercenary commands. Individual pilots quickly discovered that replacing the large pulse laser with an extended-range PPC transformed the design into a highly capable sniper, and this TR2 field modification became widespread. The Word of Blake developed the TR3 variant, mounting an improved C3 computer to make the Wraith a fast, mobile network node for their C3i-equipped formations.

The Jihad brought catastrophe to the Wraith's production. On 26 February 3080, forces from the Principality of Regulus bombarded Paradise with thousands of cobalt-laced strategic nuclear weapons, destroying the Curtiss Militech factory and rendering the planet uninhabitable. The attack killed over a hundred million civilians and left Curtiss Hydroponics in severe financial distress. The parent company announced its complete withdrawal from the military market and put the Curtiss Militech assets up for sale. No Free Worlds League company expressed interest in the Wraith's production rights, and Curtiss flatly refused to sell to the Regulans, whose destruction of Paradise had directly caused the company's ruin.

Hellespont Industries on Sian proved a willing buyer, and production began at the Hellespont 'Mech Works facility by 3087. The transition replaced existing Stinger production and scaled back Assassin manufacture to accommodate the new line. Under Capellan ownership, the Wraith became firmly associated with the Confederation Armed Forces. Hellespont engineers eventually leveraged their experience with Capellan manufacturing partners like Ceres Arms to develop new variants incorporating advanced pulse lasers and supercharger technology. The design's cultural integration into the CCAF was reflected in its informal Mandarin phoneticization, though the preferred pronunciation varied between units. The Death Commandos and Warrior Houses favored one reading while most line formations used another, a distinction that observers at the Capellan court noted extended even to the Chancellor and senior nobility.

On the arena circuits of Solaris VII, the Wraith's speed and agility made it a natural fit for gladiatorial combat. Custom modifications like the TR2-X Alexander and TR2-P Pocahontas pushed the chassis to its experimental limits, incorporating Clan technology and partial wings that would later inspire Hellespont's own Wing Wraith development program. The Wraith's journey from a water purification company's unlikely debut design to a mainstay of the Capellan military stands as one of the more remarkable manufacturing stories of the post-Clan Invasion era.

text.deployment: The Primary configuration of the Wulfen pairs a left-arm mounted Ultra Autocannon/2 with a right-arm ATM-3 launcher, providing flexible engagement capability from extreme range down to close quarters depending on ammunition selection. Both weapons are fed by a single ton of ammunition each, protected by CASE II in their respective arms. A half-ton cargo pod in the left torso provides modest logistical capacity for extended patrols. This versatile loadout makes the Prime well-suited to the reconnaissance and screening roles that define the Wulfen's primary mission profile.

The A configuration strips away all ballistic and missile weapons in favor of a single ER PPC, transforming the Wulfen into a dedicated long-range sniper. Four additional double heat sinks manage the considerable thermal load of the Clan-grade particle cannon, allowing the MechWarrior to maintain a punishing rate of fire while exploiting the chassis's speed to stay well beyond effective return range. The combination of stealth armor and a weapon capable of threatening heavier 'Mechs makes this configuration a persistent threat that opponents struggle to pin down.

The B configuration is the loadout derived from saKhan Garner Kerensky's Trial of Grievance victory over Star Colonel Josiah Ward, which silenced early opposition to the Wulfen program. Armed with an ER large laser linked to a targeting computer, the configuration delivers highly accurate fire at extended range. A supercharger and six jump jets dramatically enhance the chassis's already exceptional mobility, allowing pilots to exploit terrain and maintain optimal engagement distances. An additional double heat sink helps offset the thermal demands of sustained laser fire at high speed.

The D configuration mounts an LB 2-X autocannon in the left arm alongside an Artemis V-guided SRM-2 launcher in the right arm, both weapons supported by a ton of CASE II-protected ammunition. This loadout closely mirrors the original weapon specifications from the Wulfen's early Dark Age concept, adapted to current Clan technology standards. The combination of cluster-capable autocannon fire and precision short-range missiles gives this configuration a flexible if modest weapons suite best suited to harassment and anti-vehicle operations.

The E configuration serves as a fast generalist, blending missile and energy weapons to engage effectively across all range bands. Twin ATM-3 launchers with CASE II-protected ammunition in the right torso provide flexible ordnance delivery, while a pair of ER medium lasers and a micro pulse laser in the left arm (all linked to a targeting computer) handle close-range engagements with precision. A supercharger allows brief bursts of speed beyond the chassis's already impressive maximum velocity, giving pilots the option to rapidly close or disengage as the tactical situation demands.

The H configuration transforms the Wulfen into a powerful close-range combatant built for sustained engagements. An improved heavy large laser serves as the primary weapon, supported by a pair of improved heavy medium lasers, all mounted in the right arm. This all-energy loadout eliminates ammunition dependency, giving the configuration exceptional endurance during extended operations or deep raids where resupply is unavailable. Four additional double heat sinks help manage the substantial thermal output of the heavy laser array, though MechWarriors must still exercise fire discipline to avoid overheating during prolonged engagements.

text.overview: The Yu Huang is the premier assault command BattleMech of the Capellan Confederation. Produced by Shengli Arms on Victoria and entering service with the CCAF in 3060, the ninety-ton design was intended to serve as a symbol of Capellan martial prowess and technological resurgence under Chancellor Sun-Tzu Liao's Xin Sheng movement. Named for the Jade Emperor who rules the heavenly court in the ancient Chinese pantheon, it was commissioned as both a potent battlefield weapon and a statement of Capellan independence. Like the Ti Ts'ang before it, the Yu Huang incorporates Chinese design aesthetics and cultural elements that reinforce its role as a flagship of the Confederation's modernized military.
text.capabilities:
Built around a Chariot Type II Endo Steel frame and powered by a Hermes 360 XL engine, the Yu Huang achieves a top speed of 65 km/h, impressive for a ninety-ton assault machine. Four Rodan 90 jump jets provide 120 meters of jump capability, granting unexpected tactical mobility. Seventeen tons of Star Shell armor give the design excellent protection, though the extralight engine remains a vulnerability if either side torso is breached.

The primary armament centers on a devastating Mydron Excel LB 20-X autocannon, capable of switching between standard slugs and cluster munitions. A Ceres Arms Warrior ER PPC and Zeus LRM-10 launcher provide effective long-range engagement capability, including indirect fire support. Two Martell medium lasers and a Raker-IV medium pulse laser round out the close-range arsenal, allowing the Yu Huang to dominate at short range while remaining competent at distance.

Thirteen double heat sinks manage the thermal load adequately, though sustained fire from all weapons simultaneously can tax the cooling system. The relatively small ammunition supply for the autocannon can leave MechWarriors carefully rationing their most powerful weapon during prolonged engagements.
text.deployment: This variant is a Dark Age-era variant produced by Ceres Metals Industries on Capella, representing the latest evolution of the design. This model carries a C3 boosted master computer, enhancing command coordination beyond the standard C3 network. Its primary firepower comes from a Gauss rifle paired with a Clan-built ER PPC, combining extreme range with devastating hitting power. The incorporation of Clan technology reflects the broader trend of advanced equipment becoming available to Inner Sphere manufacturers during the late Dark Age period.
text.battleHistory:
The Yu Huang's development was part of Chancellor Sun-Tzu Liao's Xin Sheng, or "New Birth," program to modernize the Capellan Confederation Armed Forces. The Victoria facility where it was built had been discovered during the Third Succession War as a subterranean Star League-era research complex. With Word of Blake technical assistance providing the resources needed for advanced component production, the first Yu Huang entered trials in late 3059, with full production beginning in January 3060. At its debut, the Chancellor declared the design would "sit in judgment over a battlefield, meting out justice to those who would transgress against us."

Early critics questioned whether Shengli Arms could independently manufacture the LB 20-X autocannon, noting the weapon's Lyran origins. However, the Victoria facility's archives and its proximity to the Victoria Academy of Arms and Technology proved sufficient. No outside shipments were necessary, demonstrating that Capellan industry had advanced considerably since the dark days of the Fourth Succession War.

The Yu Huang saw its first major deployment during the Capellan-St. Ives War, where Warrior House Hiritsu fielded the design to devastating effect. A full lance was sent directly to Warrior House Imarra, and the Confederation began distributing the assault machine across its regiments in singles and pairs. The design earned swift respect as a command platform, and Capellan officers favored it for the combination of raw firepower and the psychological weight of its imposing, culturally significant silhouette.

Production at Victoria continued through the FedCom Civil War period, but the Jihad brought catastrophe to Shengli Arms. In December 3068, Olson's Rangers, a mercenary unit stationed on Victoria, turned against the facility without warning. The resulting attack inflicted devastating damage, and the Yu Huang production line was irreversibly destroyed. Shengli suffered capital and personnel losses of 84 percent from this single attack. While the Duan Gung and Jinggau lines were eventually restored to limited production, the Yu Huang was not rebuilt. Instead, the chambers that once housed its assembly area were repurposed for the new Dola assault BattleMech.

The loss of Victoria itself followed during the Victoria War of 3104-3105, when Federated Suns forces captured the world. Shengli Arms' remaining assets were eventually acquired by Ceres Metals Industries, which converted its Ostroc production line on Capella to produce the Yu Huang beginning around 3091. These Ceres-manufactured machines are distinguished by an elaborate head crest added by the Ceres engineers, making them instantly recognizable compared to the original Shengli-built examples. Production continues on Capella into the ilClan era, ensuring the Yu Huang remains the Confederation's signature command BattleMech.

text.overview: The Yurei is a forty-ton medium Land-Air BattleMech and the middleweight member of the Word of Blake's Spectral LAM series. Designed by Master's Wings Aerospace on Gibson and entering service in 3077, the Yurei drew its name from vengeful spirits of ancient Japanese folklore. Intended to serve as the workhorse of the three-design series alongside the lighter Pwwka and heavier Waneta, the Yurei was built exclusively for the elite Manei Domini and produced in very limited numbers. Like its stablemates, it represented a brief, final revival of LAM technology on the modern battlefield, a concept most military analysts had long considered extinct.
text.capabilities:
The Yurei is built on a Spectral-L Series YR1L chassis and powered by a Nissan 200 standard fusion engine, giving it a maximum ground speed of eighty-six kilometers per hour. Five GM ATO 100 jump jets provide a jumping range of one hundred fifty meters, with performance in aerospace fighter and AirMech modes supplemented by a single ton of fuel. A small cockpit paired with a VDNI interface allows Manei Domini pilots to manage the demanding requirements of LAM conversion, though it renders the machine effectively unusable by conventional MechWarriors.

The Yurei's armament consists entirely of Clan-grade energy weapons whose exact source remains unknown. A single Clan ER large laser serves as the primary weapon, supported by two Clan ER medium lasers. A one-ton internal bomb bay protected by CASE II provides limited ordnance delivery capability and gives the airframe a chance of surviving catastrophic internal hits. Ten double heat sinks manage the thermal load efficiently. Eight tons of Durallex Divine Protector standard armor provide solid protection for the weight class, falling just half a ton short of maximum coverage.

Despite these technologies, the Yurei remains an unremarkable performer in either BattleMech or aerospace fighter roles. Most dedicated medium designs can outrun and outgun it. Its true advantages lie in the shock value of its transformation capability, the quality of Clan weaponry squeezed into a tight frame, and the exceptional skills of its Manei Domini pilots.
text.deployment: The sole production model, this variant was deployed exclusively by Word of Blake Manei Domini formations during the final years of the Jihad. It was observed in combat only against forces from the Principality of Regulus and the Duchy of Oriente, and no variants were identified as of 3081. Given the limited engagements in which the Yurei appeared, it is possible that other configurations existed but were never encountered by coalition forces.
text.battleHistory:
The Yurei emerged from a secret Word of Blake program to revive Land-Air BattleMech technology, a field of military engineering that had been considered dead since the destruction of the last LAM factory on Irece during the Clan Invasion of 3050. The Spectral LAM series, comprising the thirty-ton Pwwka, the forty-ton Yurei, and the fifty-five-ton Waneta, were designed and built at facilities on both Gibson and Terra. The Yurei was produced at Master's Wings Aerospace on Gibson, a facility that had previously operated as the Brigadier Corporation's DropShip repair yard before the Word of Blake seized control of the planet and converted the lines for military aerospace production.

The Spectral LAM series first emerged around 3075, with the Yurei entering service approximately 3077. It enjoyed roughly a year as the most advanced design in the series before the heavier Waneta began rolling off assembly lines on Gibson and Terra. The appearance of the Spectral LAMs came as a genuine shock to both the allied coalition and the Principality of Regulus, as conventional wisdom held that LAM technology was an extinct relic of the Star League era. However, the surprise proved short-lived, and the fundamental limitations that had plagued earlier LAM designs continued to constrain the Spectral series despite its use of advanced technology and pilot augmentation.

The Yurei's production run was brutally short. In late 3078, forces from the Principality of Regulus launched a devastating assault on Gibson, conducting orbital bombardment on a planetary scale that targeted every major population center and industrial site. The Master's Wings Aerospace facility was destroyed along with virtually all other manufacturing infrastructure on the planet. With no known alternate production sites and the Word of Blake's final defeat in the Liberation of Terra, the Yurei became an effectively extinct design by 3081. What little is known about its specifications comes almost entirely from studying salvage recovered after combat engagements.
